en.title: Global Macro — Korea's chip-export boom meets China's order contraction and an energy import squeeze
en.deck: Korean October semiconductor export receipts surged as Chinese orders weakened; the official September baseline corrects the trade-surplus comparison, while OPEC+ held December production requirements.
en.regime: Concentrated AI hardware receipts alongside weak Chinese order diffusion and elevated energy import costs.
en.key_risk: High chip receipts and trade surplus obscure dependence on prices, customer capital spending and energy import unit costs.

producer_checks.information_cutoff: Initial 2026-11-01 05:00 BRT (08:00 UTC) Korea trade, NBS and last 30 October financial sessions; same-day update after official seven-country OPEC+ 1 Nov statement, before release of this revision. No fictitious Sunday financial close.
producer_checks.novelty: Distinct from October 31 China PMI: first full Korean October trade report 1 Nov (exports $115.28bn, chips $56.44bn, nonchip +34%, oil unit price +62%, physical crude volume -6.3%, region data), crosschecked to original September 1 Oct vintage ($120.94bn, +83.5% y/y, surplus $49.85bn), plus official seven OPEC+ countries Nov1 decision maintaining September required production levels for December. No new physical oil flow inferred.
producer_checks.source_check: 16 matching numbered original references per language; Korean MOTIR 1 November October trade [1] and 1 October September trade [15] separate source periods, original NBS 31 Oct PMI [2], Eurostat 30 Oct GDP and labour [3][14], original BEA 29 Oct Q3 GDP [4] and September DPI [5], verified 1 November OPEC+ primary release [16], original 4 Oct OPEC [12], dated IEA/World Bank/FAO and Fed/ECB/Treasury sources. September trade surplus 49.85-42.50 = 7.35 USD bn.
producer_checks.visual_signature: 4 bilingual matching source-linked bar charts (selected Korean exports, Sep/Oct Korea merchandise exports $120.94bn/$115.28bn, Korean crude oil import unit price +62%, physical volume -6.3%, import value +51.9%, trade destinations); one 3-chain flow, one 6-region map, one evidence table; 16 sourced bibliography entries.
producer_checks.bilingual_parity: 16 identical reference URLs, original September official exports +83.5%, surplus $49.85bn and Oct surplus $42.50bn, delta $7.35bn, exact 4 numeric chart series and parallel visuals, both include dated official OPEC+ Nov1 decision for December and Sept euro-area unemployment source [14]. Distinguishes initial morning cutoff from same-day official update.
producer_checks.research_depth: Eight H2 analytical sections per edition with three transmission pathways, two falsifiable alternative scenarios, price/volume/stock/flow distinctions; 16 primary/research and news reference URLs; four source-linked quantitative charts and one evidence table per language.
producer_checks.editorial_status: Revision 2 re-submitted for independent SHA-bound QA, addressing factual rejection and new primary November 1 OPEC+ release; no public promotion without approval and three Git SHA verification.
producer_checks.qa_handoff: Audit prior r1 rejected claims using primary Korea September 1 Oct report [15]: +83.5% export growth, merchandise surplus $49.85bn and October $42.50bn -> -$7.35bn; check October original [1] and absence of old 83.7/49.97/7.47, bilingual matching source links and chart arrays, newly verified seven-country OPEC+ 1 Nov decision December requirements vs 4 Oct decision for November [12][16]. Verify 3/3 Git blobs, no future pricing or quotas asserted as physical volumes; send only to public publisher after independent QA.

contrary_evidence: Non-semiconductor Korean exports rose 34% by value; Korea's overall October exports were below September despite faster y/y growth.
China October PMI below 50 does not prevent sharply higher Korean semiconductor exports to China.
Euro area GDP expanded 0.4% q/q and US Q3 GDP 3.4% SAAR despite weaker household real income.
Crude-oil import physical volumes fell 6.3% even as unit prices and nominal import bills rose.
September 1 October MOTIR primary data export +83.5% and surplus $49.85bn; October $42.50bn implies a decline of $7.35bn despite strong annual chip growth.
OPEC+ November 1 maintained September production requirements for December; this quota decision does not independently establish October-November physical shipment normalization.
limitations: Korean customs values cannot isolate chip volume, unit prices, ultimate users or AI customer return on capital.
No Sunday closing equity, bond, currency or commodity prices; latest completed sessions 30 Oct.
IEA September physical Hormuz flow estimate not a 1 November throughput observation.
OPEC+ November 1 official decision verified after 05 BRT morning cutoff; requirements for December do not prove compliance or physical output.
Country-level credit spreads, capital-flow attribution and food retail pass-through not established.
